one_month_reasoning: The company has not announced the Q1 FY27 report date. Past fiscal Q1 releases came on Nov 2, 2023, Nov 7, 2024 and Nov 4, 2025 (EDGAR 8-K Item 2.02 dates), and the date notice usually comes in mid-October, so the print almost certainly falls after the window. Nov 1, 2026 is a Sunday, so the effective mark is the Oct 30 close. Inside the window: late-October hyperscaler Q3 earnings and 2027 capex commentary (Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta, Amazon), the likely date announcement and pre-earnings positioning, peer prints (e.g. Ciena's and Coherent's outlook commentary), and steady 10b5-1 insider selling (the CFO sold 24,542 shares at $1,048.50 on Oct 1). The stock sits at a 52-week high after a ~20% four-day run, so momentum and short-term reversal roughly cancel. I use a near-symmetric lognormal with median ~$1,082 (a hair below spot for the insider-supply overhang) and a one-month log-sd of 0.22, a little below 97%/3.5 because no earnings fall in the window.

fair_value.method: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 ~$34.8 x 33x + $10.7/sh net cash = ~$1,159 (weight 0.5). FY28 EPS $32.6 x 36x + net cash = ~$1,184 (weight 0.3). NTM EBITDA ~$4.5B x 22x + net cash on 103M shares = ~$972 (weight 0.2). Blended ~$1,130, about 4% above spot.

reasoning: Round 2, primary-document lane. The supervisor established three facts that affect my numbers. (1) Current consensus is ~$19.8-21.8 for FY27 (MarketBeat; StockAnalysis $21.78 from 24 analysts) and ~$33 for FY28, so my round-1 FY28 of $29.5 was ~10% low. I re-anchored the quarterly path to FY27 $21.3, FY28 $32.6 and Oct-2027 NTM $34.8, one point under consensus as a haircut for pricing and concentration. (2) Net cash of $1.10B ($10.7/sh) belongs in the value. Checked against the 10-K and 8-K balance sheet: converts $1,554M with cash-settled principal, plus ~$83M term loans. (3) Use ~103M diluted shares rather than my 101-105M; this is immaterial to per-share EPS. A 12-peer comp set (optical hardware COHR/CIEN/FN/MTSI/GLW; AI-interconnect silicon MRVL/CRDO/ALAB/AVGO; systems ANET/APH/CLS) has a median forward P/E of 36.7x (range 20.5-62.4) and a median derived forward EV/EBITDA of 22.4x. LITE is at 49.8x FY27 consensus and ~33x FY28. LITE's faster growth, 40% operating margin and net cash argue for a premium; its concentration, component-cycle exposure and peak-cycle EPS argue against one. I apply 33x to Oct-2027 NTM EPS (a ~10% evidence-based discount to the median), 36x to FY28 and 22x to NTM EBITDA. The legs give $1,159, $1,184 and $972, blended to ~$1,130, ~4% above spot. Fair value rose from $1,000 on the consensus-anchored EPS, net cash and the move of my multiple toward the 12-peer median. Distribution: median ~$1,100, a little below fair value because peer multiples are themselves at AI-cycle highs. Log-sd is 0.70 on the downside and 0.64 on the upside, against 97% realized vol, since part of last year's move was a one-off rerating; optical names' 60-75% cycle drawdowns keep the left tail fat. P(close >= $1,085) is 0.51, up from 0.48 in round 1. Research limits: Twelve Data statistics needs a higher plan and Alpha Vantage was rate-limited, so peer multiples come from StockAnalysis pages (2026-10-02 close) and forward EV/EBITDA is my derivation. The 24 comp data pages are off-lane by nature and push the in-lane share of the source list below 60%; excluding the required comps and consensus data pages, 8 of 12 sources are in lane, and the core valuation inputs remain primary filings.

comps_summary.method_note: Forward P/E is StockAnalysis's figure at the 2026-10-02 close. No source I could reach (Twelve Data statistics needs a higher plan, Alpha Vantage was rate-limited, StockAnalysis gives no EBITDA estimates) publishes forward EV/EBITDA, so ev_ebitda_fwd is my derivation: trailing EV/EBITDA x (forward P/E / trailing P/E). That assumes EBITDA grows in line with EPS, so treat it as approximate. Peer fiscal years differ (Apr, Jun, Oct, Nov year-ends). For high-amortisation or high-SBC names (MRVL, MTSI, ALAB), the GAAP trailing vs adjusted forward mismatch inflates the derived figure. Next-year growth for Dec-year-end peers is paywalled beyond FY26, so the current-year consensus or a derived EPS growth is shown and labelled.
comps_summary.lite_today: LITE trades at 49.8x consensus FY27 EPS of $21.78 (StockAnalysis) and ~33x FY28 consensus of ~$33, against a 36.7x 12-peer median and a 20.5-62.4x range. Only ALAB is higher. My rough forward EV/EBITDA for LITE is ~36x (EV $96.3B / FY27 EBITDA of ~$2.7B, which assumes $6.34B consensus revenue at ~40% operating margin plus D&A), against a 22.4x peer median.
comps_summary.lite_in_my_methods: P/E leg 1: 33x NTM EPS at Oct-2027, about 10% below the 36.7x peer median, inside the 20.5-62.4x range. P/E leg 2: 36x FY28, about the median. EV/EBITDA leg: 22x NTM EBITDA, about the 22.4x median. LITE today is 49.8x FY27 consensus (above all peers but ALAB) and ~33x FY28.
comps_summary.justification: Of my three legs, only the NTM P/E leg sits off the median: about a 10% discount (33x vs 36.7x). I argue it is persistent through Oct-2027 on evidence, not on sell-side calls. (1) Cyclicality: LITE is a component supplier whose earnings swing with the optical cycle. Revenue was $1.65B in FY25 against $3.01B in FY26, the company was GAAP loss-making on a trailing basis (StockAnalysis shows no trailing P/E), and FY24 revenue fell, as Coherent's did (-8.8%). The NTM EPS I capitalise in Oct-2027 is a scarcity-priced peak (a ~50% gross margin on EML/InP shortage) facing new InP capacity. Less cyclical peers (APH, ANET) earn 28-43% operating margins through the cycle. (2) Concentration: two customers were 41.6% of FY26 revenue (10-K), far above diversified peers such as APH, GLW and CLS. (3) Returns: LITE's ROIC over a cycle has been low (FY24-25 losses), while the high-multiple peers (ANET ROIC 285%, ALAB 63%) have structurally higher returns. Against that, LITE's next-year growth (revenue +110%, EPS +151%) is the fastest in the set, its ~40% guided operating margin is near the top, and it has $1.1B net cash, so I do not discount the full-year FY28 leg or the EBITDA leg. Net, I use about 34x on a weighted basis, roughly 7% below the median. The median itself is inflated by AI-cycle multiples (MRVL, ALAB and MTSI at 90-170x trailing), so I would not pay above it. Round-1 30x sat below the 12-peer median without a persistence argument; I have moved it toward the median and recorded that in revisions.
comps_summary.peer_set_note: There are 12 peers: 5 optical hardware and components makers (COHR, CIEN, FN, MTSI, GLW), 4 AI-interconnect silicon makers (MRVL, CRDO, ALAB, AVGO) and 3 networking or interconnect systems and manufacturing names (ANET, APH, CLS). AAOI is excluded because it has negative TTM EBITDA and GAAP earnings and no forward estimate is visible, so its multiples are not meaningful. Chinese transceiver makers (InnoLight, Eoptolink) are excluded because no cited source covered them.
